title: Synchronous and asynchronous communication between services

videos.script: When one service needs something from another, it can ask and wait, or it can say what it wants and get on with its day. {{two}} The first is synchronous. It is how function calls work, and how HTTP works by default. It is simple to write and simple to follow. {{sync}} It also ties the caller to everything behind it. If the service you call is slow, you are slow. If it is down, you are down. {{coupling}} In this lesson you build a chain of three services on your machine and measure exactly that. The delays add up. The failures travel back up the chain. {{chain}} You will make the last one slow and watch the first one wait, and then give the middle one a timeout and watch it stop waiting. {{timeout}} Then the other way. A request accepted at once, and the work done later, with the client asking for the result when it is ready. {{async}} Asynchronous communication buys independence in time. It is paid for in things you have to think about: answers that arrive later, in a different order, or twice. {{cost}} The next two lessons take that bill item by item. This one is about knowing which of the two styles a conversation needs.
